transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-09-15 15:00 PT
Duration: 55 minutes
Attendees: Samir (Redwood AE), Lina (Redwood SE), Evan (Redwood CSM), Maria (ZenHealth CTO), Jonah (ZenHealth SecEng), Priya (ZenHealth Legal), Amit (Platform)

Summary:
Quick review of third-party pen test results delivered last week; discussion focused on high/critical findings, remediation timelines, vulnerability management process, secure SDLC and patching cadence, plus SOC2/ISO evidence and KMS/encryption questions. Agreed to share prioritized findings and schedule follow-up deep-dive.

Topics:
- Pen test high/critical findings and remediation status
- Vulnerability management and tracking (Jira, SLAs)
- Secure SDLC (SCA, dependency scanning, PR gating)
- Patching cadence and emergency patch SLA
- RBAC/SSO and audit logs retention
- Encryption at rest/ KMS architecture and key management
- Data residency and segmentation for PHI

Transcript:
[00:00] Samir: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick around the room, then Lina will walk through the pen test topline.
[00:20] Maria: Hi all, Maria here. We're particularly focused on the critical items that might touch PHI, so appreciate the prioritization.
[00:30] Lina: Great, thanks. I pulled the redacted report and we highlighted 3 critical, 6 high, remainder medium/low. The critical ones relate to an exposed admin endpoint in the legacy analytics svc, an outdated OpenSSL build on one internal cluster node, and an auth bypass scenario when SSO is unavailable and fallback auth chips in.
[00:58] Jonah: Can you clarify which cluster hosts the OpenSSL issue? Is that customer-facing or internal only?
[01:08] Lina: It's an internal cluster used for batch ETL, not directly customer-facing, but it processes PHI in some jobs. The node is in us-east-1 and was missed by automated patching because it was cordoned during a maintenance window.
[01:28] Samir: Important callout about the cordoned node; we've seen that pattern before where maintenance state skips the patch run. For follow-up we usually suggest adding a tiling check in orchestration to ensure nodes come back uncordoned before patch window ends.
[01:46] Amit: That would help. Our ops run monthly patch windows, but urgency for critical CVEs is immediate; what's Redwood's recommended SLA for emergency patches?
[01:59] Lina: For customer-managed infra we recommend emergency patching within 72 hours for critical CVEs, with a documented rollback plan. For Redwood Dedicated customers we can offer quicker coordinated rollouts as part of the support add-on.
[02:14] Maria: Okay, we'll need that in writing for our security committee.
[02:22] Lina: Noted; Samir I'll include that in the follow-up emails.
[02:28] Samir: Yep. Next critical item: exposed admin endpoint. We detected unauthenticated access to an older admin path that's still accessible via routing rules. The pen tester used an old proxy to hit it.
[02:45] Jonah: That one worries me. Is that in the same svc as the public UI?
[02:50] Lina: Different service, legacy analytics. Short-term mitigation is to add an IP allowlist and strict RBAC checks, long-term we recommend decommissioning the path and moving functionality behind authenticated routes.
[03:05] Priya: From a compliance standpoint, we need evidence that access is restricted and an attestation timeline. Can Redwood provide sample RBAC audit logs showing deny events?
[03:18] Samir: We can export audit logs for request denies and RBAC changes. We don't have ZenHealth's logs, but we can show sample redwood audit trails and the retention settings. We'll also share docs on configuring audit log retention to meet SOC 2 requirements.
[03:33] Maria: Good. Also question on KMS: pen test flagged that some backups in the internal pipeline were encrypted with a locally-managed key repository. We try to keep keys in a managed KMS. What are Redwood's key management recommendations?
[03:48] Lina: We recommend using a cloud KMS with envelope encryption and customer-managed keys where customers require separation of duties. For Private deployments we support HSM integrations. For snapshots/backups we recommend at-rest encryption with CMEK and rotate keys at least annually.
[04:05] Jonah: Do you publish key rotation procedures or admin role separation docs?
[04:10] Lina: Yes, we'll share the KMS integration guide and sample IAM policies.
[04:15] Samir: Also worth noting we support external KMS references in the config so the key never lands in our control plane for certain private deployments.
[04:26] Maria: That helps. On data residency, the pen test noted some processing jobs running in us-east while policy requires EU for PHI. Are there options to pin processing to eu-west-1?
[04:38] Samir: Yes, customers can request region pinning. For Dedicated/Private we can ensure workers are provisioned in EU regions. We'll need a list of datasets you deem regulated so we can map job selectors.
[04:50] Amit: I'll provide that list.
[04:53] Jonah: About vulnerability management, what's Redwood's cadence for dependency scanning and SCA in the build pipeline?
[04:59] Lina: We run SCA on every PR in our pipeline, weekly SBOM reconcilation, and monthly full image scans. We also consume feeds for new CVE disclosures and elevate critical ones. For customers we can provide scan artifacts and SBOM exports on request.
[05:16] Maria: Do you integrate with Jira for automatically opening remediation tickets?
[05:20] Lina: We have integrations; we can push findings to Jira or ServiceNow and set SLA workflows. That might help ZenHealth track remediation windows.
[05:28] Jonah: Great. For the pen test findings we want a clear remediation SLA: critical 7 days to mitigate or start mitigation, high 30 days, medium 90 days. Does Redwood recommend similar timelines?
[05:40] Lina: Those are reasonable. From Redwood's perspective for hosted APIs we push hotfixes faster; for customer infra we recommend 72 hours for critical to begin mitigation, 7 days to implement fix if possible. We'll document recommended SLAs in the follow-up.
[05:56] Priya: Legal also wants to confirm that audit logs are tamper-evident and retention meets 2 years for incident investigations for our SOC2 scope.
[06:08] Samir: We support immutable log export to customer-owned S3 buckets with MFA delete and can provide log signing options. Retention policy is configurable; we'll include configuration steps and a sample retention policy that meets 2 years.
[06:23] Maria: On the auth fallback bypass, sounds like when SSO IdP is unreachable the system falls back to local auth and a misconfig allowed session fixation. Is the recommendation to disable fallback entirely?
[06:35] Lina: Yes, either disable fallback or enforce step-up auth so that fallback cannot grant admin roles. Also add monitoring for unusual auth patterns.
[06:44] Jonah: We'll prefer disabling fallback for admin roles. For low-priv users maybe a different path.
[06:50] Samir: We'll capture that as a configuration best-practice and include a checklist you can run against your deployment.
[06:57] Maria: Regarding secure SDLC, what does Redwood do for PR gating? Are there mandatory checks for secrets scanning and SCA?
[07:07] Lina: Mandatory checks include secrets scanning, SCA, unit test coverage thresholds, and required approvers for certain repos. We can share our secure SDLC policy and sample GitHub branch protection rules.
[07:19] Amit: Do you run dynamic scans on staging before release?
[07:22] Lina: Yes, we run nightly DAST against staging and smoke run on each release candidate.
[07:27] Jonah: What about third-party dependencies in models and tokenizers? Those are often pulled in via pip wheels; do you SCA those as well?
[07:35] Lina: We include runtime deps in SCA and produce SBOMs for model-serving images; we also have a process for vetting model artifacts for known vulnerabilities.
[07:45] Maria: Good. On remediation verification, can Redwood re-run the original pen test checks after ZenHealth patches?
[07:53] Samir: We can run verification scans and let you use our test harness to validate fixes, or we can coordinate with your 3rd-party tester for an after-action verification.
[08:03] Jonah: We'll likely want Redwood to run an internal verification first.
[08:07] Samir: Fine. We'll provision a verification scan and share results.
[08:11] Priya: For compliance evidence we need SOC2 Type II and ISO27001 artifacts; you mentioned sharing earlier.
[08:18] Samir: I'll share links to our compliance portal and redact any sensitive customer references. We'll include scope and any subservice org notes.
[08:26] Maria: Also want to ensure encryption in transit and at rest are demonstrated for backups and replication.
[08:33] Lina: TLS for all control and data planes, and CMEK for storage; we'll include architecture diagram that shows encryption boundaries.
[08:41] Maria: On the backlog, do you recommend short-term mitigations that don't require a full refactor?
[08:47] Lina: Yes. For the admin endpoint, short term: firewall rules, strict RBAC, and decommission plan. For OpenSSL node: isolate and rotate creds, patch node, and run image rebuild. For auth fallback: disable fallback for admin roles and add monitoring.
[09:02] Amit: What's the expected effort for each? Rough estimates please.
[09:06] Lina: Firewall/RBAC changes a few engineer-days. OpenSSL patching one day plus verification, image rebuild a few days. Auth fallback change and testing a couple of days. Exact estimates depend on your change control process.
[09:20] Maria: We'll need these on a timeline to present to our security committee next week.
[09:25] Samir: We'll produce a proposed remediation timeline and owners as an appendix to the pen test pack.
[09:31] Jonah: For patching cadence, we currently do monthly patches and emergency patches ad-hoc. Is it worth moving to weekly for certain critical hosts?
[09:41] Lina: For hosts that process PHI you might want a faster cadence or at least host-class-based policies. Weekly patching for critical clusters is reasonable. Also ensure automated canary deploys and rolling restarts to avoid missed nodes.
[09:55] Maria: Action items and next steps?
[09:58] Samir: Quick recap: we will share the redacted pen test PDF, an exported prioritized vuln list (Lina), SOC2/ISO docs (Samir), KMS and RBAC config guides (Lina), and a proposed remediation timeline. Customer to provide regulated dataset list and current patching docs. We'll schedule a technical deep-dive next week.
[10:20] Priya: Thanks all. Please mark action items and due dates.
[10:24] Samir: Will do. Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the attachments.

End of transcript.

References mentioned: redacted_pen_test_report.pdf (shared), SOC2_portal_link (to be shared), KMS_integration_guide.pdf, RBAC_audit_sample_logs.csv, remediation_timeline_draft.xlsx
